speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: asked the Prime Minister when individuals publicise complaints or petitions to Government agencies which may contain inaccuracies (a) what are the considerations behind whether Government agencies may publicly disclose identifying information and personal details of these individuals; (b) what safeguards exist to ensure that only the minimum personal information is disclosed to establish the facts of the case; and (c) what can be done to ensure that individuals with genuine grievances or unmet needs are not deterred from seeking help publicly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Otherwise, if citizens are misled about the Government’s processes or policies, they may become unnecessarily anxious or may make decisions that are detrimental to themselves based on the incorrect information, for example, deciding not to seek medical treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Such disclosure of personal data by Government agencies is limited in scope.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Third, care is taken not to disclose personal data that is irrelevant to the case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Government is committed to putting citizens at the heart of all we do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Citizens have many channels to request for help from the Government and to give feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These include physical touchpoints, such as service centres and online channels, such as the OneService app and emails of Quality Service Managers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Government treats all feedback seriously, whether that feedback is conveyed publicly or via one of these channels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We will take the necessary action to address the issue and close the loop with the member of the public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I am quite concerned we will discourage persons who are trying to get help because these cases can be publicised for reasons beyond the complainant's control.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Someone may put up a private Facebook post and find that it gets shared, and they do not know why it got shared.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And only if that does not happen, then, as a last resort, the agency could clarify matters without that person's consent.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The issue at hand is, of course, that these types of public declarations, whether anonymised or not, are going to be unusual in nature.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is something about the case or the complainant or the interaction, which does not quite fall into Standard Operating Procedure, nor lend itself to a protocol; otherwise, we would not be in this situation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Thirdly, in a way, which as the Member had pointed out, may open itself to manipulation and further downstream ambiguity, disinformation, whether inadvertently or deliberately.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I think I have articulated in my answer the principles under which public sector agencies are expected to operate; the principles which citizens can expect of the Government in dealing with this matter.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State if the Government has channels and measures for citizens who want to seek redress against the Government for what they deem as unfair public disclosure since the Government is not bound by the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Certainly, there are many numbers of channels and feedback routes which I have described in my previous answer.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Citizens can approach their Member of Parliament, they can approach anybody and they can use any of these means, including a public discourse, should they wish to pursue the matter.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is merely that, should a complaint occur in the public space and as a result of that complaint, the public has been misinformed, inaccuracies have been stated, then those inaccuracies need to be stated in public in a way that is unambiguous and the facts robustly explained to everybody.
